https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4691.title: Beneath the Surface
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4691.speaker: Cormac Parker Jr.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4691.blurb: We’ve all been at that lunch where one person says the thing no one else dared to. This week, Jesus is that person. The ones who invited him never saw it coming. In Luke 11:37-54 Jesus pulls back the surface and reveals it’s possible to appear faithful and still miss the heart of God: justice, mercy, love and care for people. How do we know when we’ve missed God’s Heart?

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4690.blurb: Jesus makes it clear that there is no middle ground. As the kingdom of God advances and the power of Satan crumbles, we are called to choose where our allegiance lies. The beauty and the power of the gospel invite us to the same choice every time: choose Jesus.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4690.speaker: Dan Westman
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4690.title: No Middle Ground

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4689.blurb: Prayer was never meant to be a password whispered to a distant God. In Luke 11, Jesus invites us beyond formula and into a relationship, where ordinary needs, deepest fears, and unanswered questions all have a place. Here prayer is marked by a surprising boldness rooted in who is on the other side of the door.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4689.raw_title: On The Other Side of The Door - Luke
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4689.speaker: Cormac Parker Jr.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4689.title: On The Other Side of The Door

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4686.blurb: Jesus says that “one thing is necessary”: “the good portion.” Yes, but what is it?
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4686.title: One Necessary Thing

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4687.blurb: We are called to obedience to God, but we need more than obedience. In Luke 10:25-37, which includes one of Jesus’ best-known parables, we get it.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4687.title: More Than Obedience

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4685.blurb: Jesus sends us out into the world to share his love to others, and though our expectations need to be set rightly, there is only joy at the end of the mission.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4685.raw_title: The Joy of the Mission - Luke
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4685.title: The Joy of the Mission

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4684.blurb: Jesus promises us that following him won’t be easy. But is it worth it? Luke 9:51-62 opens us to enormous possibilities.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4684.title: Set Your Face

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4683.blurb: There's a scoreboard most of us keep that no one else can see. It’s always running. Who's ahead, who's behind, where we land. We measure it with titles, schools, feeds, paychecks. Twelve men once had that argument out loud, about which of them was the greatest. Jesus was on his way to a cross, he answered them with a child.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4683.title: G.O.A.T.

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4682.blurb: The glory of Jesus is revealed on the mountain. The need for Jesus is revealed in the valley. As the disciples confront a surprising failure, we see how moments of weakness can become unexpected invitations to trust Jesus more deeply.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4682.title: Down from the Mountain

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4681.blurb: We all long for mountaintop moments with God—times when his presence feels especially real. But what are those moments actually for? And what do we do when they seem elusive? In Luke 9, one mountaintop encounter between Jesus and his disciples reminds us that whether we find ourselves on the mountain, in the valley, or somewhere in between, Jesus is inviting us to see him more clearly and follow him more faithfully.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4681.raw_title: On the Mountaintop with Jesus - Luke
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4681.title: On the Mountaintop with Jesus

https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4680.blurb: Jesus tells us how to “save” ourselves. How do we do it? The way is counterintuitive and paradoxical. It’s also revolutionary.
https://pbc.org?enmse_mid=4680.title: Take Up Your Cross
